_comment: Spark-X2.5-4B (Q8_0) as ARJUN's orchestrator — the model that runs the chat. Merge the entry below into <app data>/models/registry.json, or copy this file over it if you have no other declared models. The id is tagged 'orchestrator.' so it is elected without an administrator having to choose in Models; a choice made in Models always outranks this tag. See docs/models/spark-x2-5-orchestrator.md for what each field was measured from, and why contextLength is what it is.

models._comment: contextLength is the model's TRAINED window, not the window it will be served at. ARJUN's vram_planner walks down from here to the largest window the card can actually hold: measured on an RTX 5060 Laptop (7.9 GB) that is 65 536; on a 16 GB card 524 288; on 24 GB the full 1 048 576. Declaring the trained figure is what lets the planner make that choice per machine — declaring a smaller one would cap every machine at the weakest one's answer.
models.name: Spark-X2.5 4B (Q8_0)
models._comment_revision: The publisher revision these bytes were taken from, not a branch or a download alias. XHToken/Spark-X2.5-4B-GGUF. An alias names a different file whenever the publisher re-uploads, so evidence citing one cites nothing; the sha256 proves THESE bytes and this says where they came from. Verified on this machine: 4,375,021,152 bytes hashing to the sha256 above.
models._comment_min_llama_build: spark2_5 was added to llama.cpp in b10828. A build older than that does not fail gracefully — it reports an unknown architecture after reading the whole file. ARJUN checks this before launching and refuses with both numbers named, rather than substituting a different model or quantisation.
models._comment_classifications: Empty means this model is cleared for NOTHING until somebody decides otherwise. That is the registry's safety property and it is deliberately not pre-filled here: an administrator who has reviewed this model's provenance adds the classifications it may be used on, for example ["internal", "processDiagram"].
models._comment_sampling: Defaults the managed server is started with, applied to any request that does not state its own. Low temperature because this model's job is orchestration: tool-call arguments have to come out as valid JSON against a schema every time, and that is worth more here than variety. The model's own header suggests temp 1.0 / top_p 0.95, which is a chat default rather than an agent one.
